look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · Small UNARMED black-nightshade herb with alternate ovate leaves, tiny white 5-lobed flowers and SHORT yellow anthers. The truly decisive field comparison is with MATURE fruit: S. emulans has GREEN CALYX LOBES APPRESSED/SPREADING against berry base and a fruiting PEDICEL that commonly drops with the berry; S. americanum has strongly REFLEXED calyx lobes and its fruit pedicel generally remains on plant. Photo 2 shows only an IMMATURE GREEN berry—do not overidentify from that.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted species is documented from Texas by FNA/POWO; county verification paused; user explicitly requested encounter-based look-alike learner.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Not a verified Hays County native/occurrence, do not feed county-specific scores.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae: fused 5-lobed corolla, five anthers, berry fruit; this unarmed black-nightshade complex has simple alternate leaves, unlike prickly buffalobur.
best_field_traits: Unarmed green annual or short-lived perennial; simple alternate ovate leaves, entire to shallowly toothed or wavy.
Tiny white five-lobed rotate/star corollas, usually small unbranched flower clusters.
Yellow short anthers typically ~1.0–1.5 mm in FNA, with relatively LONGER free filaments ~0.6–1.0 mm than S. americanum.
Mature berries globose, ca. 5–10 mm, dull or only slightly glossy purplish-black; immature berries green are NOT diagnostic.
Fruiting calyx has small lobes APPRESSED or SPREADING against berry rather than strongly curling back.
Fruit-bearing pedicels often reflexed/recurved, thickened at the apex; the mature berry normally falls WITH its stalk.
Often 6–9 sclerotic granules (hard stone cells) within berry; specialist character requiring safe specimen handling, NOT tasting.
morphology_keys.habit: Small unarmed green branching herb common in disturbed places. Absence of prickles alone rules out buffalobur but not similar Morelloid black nightshades.
morphology_keys.leaf: Simple alternate ovate to elliptic blades, edges entire, wavy or shallowly toothed. Leaf undersides may be purple tinged but color is variable and not reliable alone.
morphology_keys.flower: Small white five-part star corollas, five little yellow anthers (~1.0–1.5 mm according to Flora of North America) with free filaments about 0.6–1.0 mm. Visible anther and filament measurements need macro scale; non-diagnostic wilted flower photos only show shape and placement.
morphology_keys.fruit: Dark purple-black, commonly dull or only slightly glossy when ripe, globose, ~5–10 mm. GREEN lobes of fruiting calyx remain APPRESSED/SPREADING, not strongly reflexed. Fruit stalk often reflexed/curved and may fall WITH mature berry; pedicel apex thickens.
morphology_keys.habitat: Moist woods, stream banks, gardens, roadsides and disturbed areas. Texas reported by Flora of North America, but Hays county range/occurrence has NOT been audited.
morphology_keys.management: Treat as a field ID subject only; do not recommend eating leaves or fruits based on photographs because black-nightshade confusion and glycoalkaloids present risk.

field_terms.anther: Pollen-producing yellow tip of a stamen; look at free filament length below it, not corolla size alone.
field_terms.filament: Slender stalk of a stamen below the anther. S. emulans filaments are relatively longer than those of S. americanum.
field_terms.calyx: Five green sepals under the flower or fruit; APPRESSED means held against berry; REFLEXED means bent back away from it.
field_terms.pedicel: Single flower/fruit stalk; dropping with the berry differs from fruit detaching alone.
field_terms.stone_cells: Hard internal non-seed sclerotic granules, often 6–9 in S. emulans; advanced taxonomic character, not an eating recommendation.

crew_field_sequence: 1 · Find UNARMED leafy plant with simple alternate ovate leaves; rule out prickly Solanum.
2 · Look at tiny white flowers: photograph the YELLOW ANTHERS and especially their free filaments with a millimeter scale.
3 · IMMATURE GREEN fruit cannot confirm species; return later for a mature berry and its green base.
4 · MATURE FRUIT: side macro showing the five small green calyx lobes APPRESSED/SPREADING on berry base, not bent backwards.
5 · PEDICEL: photograph intact ripe clusters and fallen berry WITH/without attached pedicel. S. emulans typically drops WITH stalk, S. americanum leaves stalk behind.
6 · Compare: longer flower anthers (>~2 mm) point toward S. nigrescens/interius; short anthers plus strongly BACKWARD ripe calyx point toward S. americanum.
7 · Without measured flower and mature fruit calyx, record Solanum morelloid group instead of guessing exact species.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Never split S. emulans and S. americanum from black berry or small white flower alone; inspect short anthers/filaments + mature calyx orientation + fruiting pedicels.

field_matrix.flower: Small white star; short anthers ~1–1.5 mm, relatively longer free filaments ~0.6–1 mm
field_matrix.berries: Dull or somewhat shiny purple-black, about 5–10 mm
field_matrix.calyx: APPRESSED to SPREADING under ripe fruit
field_matrix.pedicels: Typically reflexed/recurved, thickened apex; drops WITH ripe berry
field_matrix.quick_rule: SHORT anthers + appressed fruit calyx + fruit drops with stalk.

field_matrix.flower: Very short plump yellow anthers; free filaments shorter
field_matrix.calyx: STRONGLY REFLEXED away from ripe berry
field_matrix.pedicels: Generally erect/spreading, often remain AFTER ripe fruit falls
field_matrix.quick_rule: Shiny black + calyx turned back + fruit leaves stalk.
Anther length distinguishes when calyx overlaps.

field_matrix.taxon: Solanum interius · CENTRAL PLAINS BLACK NIGHTSHADE
field_matrix.berries: Usually LARGER than emulans, often ~10–14 mm
field_matrix.quick_rule: Longer anthers and larger berries; possibly closer Great Plains overlap.

field_matrix.pedicels: Compare internal fruits, seed and stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Introduced comparison; avoid ID from black berry alone.

not_reliable_alone: White star flower and alternate leaves: all close black nightshades share them.
Small anthers: S. americanum also has small anthers.
One GREEN IMMATURE fruit or its calyx: does not prove mature calyx pattern.
Dull versus glossy berry without lighting control: imperfect; combine with calyx, pedicels and flower.
Historical name S. ptychanthum was applied to S. emulans by older regional literature, but its type now belongs to S. americanum; do not silently transfer photos by that name without vouchers.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: SHORT anthers + calyx APPRESSED on fully ripe berry + ripe fruit may fall with its pedicel. Do not call it from a green berry.

items.why_it_matters: Teach that a single close calyx is insufficient when S. nigrescens is possible.
